reference_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(t.n_products), 2) AS avg_products
FROM (
  -- one row per order
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS n_products
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
) AS t
alternatives:
WITH order_products AS (
  -- one row per order
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS n_products
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n_products), 2) AS avg_products
FROM order_products

SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT pairs.order_id), 2) AS avg_products
FROM (
  -- one row per order and product
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id, product_id
  FROM order_lines
) AS pairs

other_way.sql:
SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT pairs.order_id), 2) AS avg_products
FROM (
  -- one row per order and product
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id, product_id
  FROM order_lines
) AS pairs
other_way.tradeoff: Counting distinct order and product pairs per order gives the same average, but the per-order grain is less visible.
